validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and independently confirmed. This is the fourth parallel trunk line (Uzbek: 'chetvertaya nitka') in the Gazli-Kagan corridor -- the sheet's own segment_name 'Segment IV' is correct. Three independent, non-GEM sources (Sputnik uz.sputniknews.ru 2021-11-29; Uzreport.news 2021-05-21, 'K 2023 godu v Uzbekistane postroyat 315 km magistralnykh gazoprovodov'; Trend.Az/az 2021, English) all report a NEW 140 km Gazli-Kagan main-line under construction as part of Uzbekistan's 2021-2023 gas-transmission modernization program -- exact 3-way agreement on 140 km. Sputnik additionally states this fourth line will carry an ADDITIONAL 25 million cubic meters/day and quotes ~100 of the 140 km already built by Nov 2021; also states lines I and II date to 1973-1983 and line III opened 2006, so a fourth, separate physical line built 2021-2023 is exactly what the roster records at P3983 (distinct from P2290 and P3984, which correspond to the earlier lines/reconstructions -- no duplicate). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a Magistralny gazoprovod (main/trunk transmission line) per every source -- PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both confirmed. DUPLICATE: none -- P3983's 140 km / new-build / 2021-2023 signature does not match P2290 (115.3 km, mixed 720/1020 mm -- reads as the reconstructed Line I/II, per a 2020-era note that 720 mm pipe was replaced with 1020 mm on the 27-78 km section) or P3984 (116 km, 1020 mm -- a different, already-operating line). No source describes P3983 as the same pipe as another roster row. LENGTH: CONFIRMED, 140.00 km, high tier (3 independent sources, exact agreement, none GEM-derived). CAPACITY: CONFIRMED, 25.00 mill.Sm3/day, medium tier (Sputnik states it explicitly and precisely; no second source gives a capacity figure for this specific line, so single-source but from a substantive dated news article, not a wire republish). DIAMETER -- MATERIAL DISAGREEMENT: Uztransgaz's own 2022 ESG/sustainability report (utg.uz, verified live, PDF) lists, under its investment-program section, projects 'ready for tie-in after construction' ('gotovye k vrezke posle stroitelstva'): 'Magistralny gazoprovod «Gazli - Kagan» Du 1220 mm 140 km' -- the SAME 140 km figure, same pipeline name, described as freshly built and awaiting connection (matching P3983's 2021-2023 construction timeline and 2023 StartYear1) -- but at 1220 mm, not the 1020 mm currently on the sheet. Note the document ALSO separately lists 'Gazli - Kagan I nitka Du 1020 mm uchastok 78-112 km protyazhennostyu 34 km' as a different, 34 km RECONSTRUCTED section of the older Line I -- i.e. the 1020 mm figure on the sheet plausibly comes from that adjacent line item being conflated with the new 140 km Line IV. Verification note: the automated url_verifier FAILed a direct '1220' substring check on this same PDF (a known large-PDF extraction-reach limitation documented in the script's own header -- the '140' token happens to appear earlier in the document, on an axis label, while '1220' sits ~page 18/120 and the extractor doesn't reach that far); manually confirmed with `pdftotext -layout` on the full downloaded PDF, which shows the exact line quoted above. Only one source states 1220 mm (no second, independent source was found affirming either figure) so this is flagged, not silently applied. OWNER: Uztransgaz 100% is plausible and unopposed -- Uztransgaz JSC is Uzbekistan's sole state trunk gas-transmission operator, and the same 2022 ESG report lists this exact pipeline project as part of ITS OWN investment/modernization program (i.e. Uztransgaz identifies the asset as its own). Not independently corroborated by a second, separate origin -- see fills, tier medium. STATUS: current 'operating' is plausible; see status_reviews. Housekeeping: every existing [ref] cell on this row (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Start, Capacity) cites the same utg.uz press URL, which is a genuine 404 (Uztransgaz press-service URLs rot fast); a Wayback capture (timestamp 20260211121103) exists per the availability API but web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this machine all of 2026-08-26 (a network condition, not evidence of anything) so it could not be read or cited today -- do not treat that as a deletion, and re-attempt the Wayback read on a later pass before dropping the ref.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched Russian-language sources for a specific 2023+ tie-in/commissioning announcement (queries for 'chetvertaya nitka zapushchena/vvedena 2023', president-attended launch events, kun.uz/gazeta.uz/podrobno.uz coverage) and found none -- no dated press event marking the pipe going live. However: (1) Sputnik (2021-11-29) shows ~100/140 km already built with the modernization program targeting completion 'k 2023 godu' (Uzreport.news, Trend.Az); (2) Uztransgaz's own 2022 ESG report (published 2023-08-29, the most recent dated independent evidence found) lists the 140 km line under 'gotovye k vrezke posle stroitelstva' -- construction complete, awaiting final tie-in -- which is consistent with a StartYear1=2023 operational start shortly after the report's writing; (3) a later web search snippet noted 'as of August 2024 there have not been any updates about the project,' consistent with a completed, quietly-operating asset generating no further news, not with a stalled/dormant one. No shelving, cancellation, or delay signal found anywhere. This is short of a definitive launch-day confirmation, but the trajectory (built -> ready for tie-in as of Aug 2023 -> no negative signal since) supports confirming the recorded operating status rather than flagging it stale; the dormancy rules (stale-2y/4y) apply to proposed/shelved states, not to a build-out that reached 'ready for tie-in' and then simply stopped generating separate news, which is the normal pattern for a completed trunk line.
